part1.instruction: Choose the correct words and write them on the lines. There is one example.

part2.title: Part 2 – Short Dialogues
part2.instruction: Read the dialogues and choose the best answer (A, B or C). There is one example.

example.question: Where did you go after school today, Tom?
options: A) I went to the park.
B) I am going to the park.
C) I go to the park every day.

part3.title: Part 3 – Complete the Story
part3.instruction: Read the story. Choose a word from the box. Write the correct word next to numbers 1–5. There is one example.
part3.storyText: Last summer, Sam and his family went on a special trip to visit a famous [example: cave] in the mountains near their town. Sam had never been (1) ________ before, and he was very (2) ________ about the whole adventure. When they arrived at the dark (3) ________ of the cave, the guide gave everyone a bright (4) ________ to carry because the tunnels inside were very dark indeed. The guide told them that the passageways were quite (5) ________ in some parts, so they had to walk carefully in a single line. Deep inside the cave, Sam noticed some incredible paintings on the rocky walls. The guide explained that these (6) ________ drawings were made by people who lived there thousands of years ago, and Sam felt very lucky to see something so special and historic.

titleQuestion.question: Now choose the best name for the story. Tick one box.
options: A family visit to a cave
titleQuestion.answer: A family visit to a cave

part4.title: Part 4 – Factual Text
part4.instruction: Read the text. Choose the right words and write them on the lines.
paragraphs: Lions are one of the most powerful wild animals (1) ________ the world. They live mainly on the open grasslands of Africa, which are called savannahs.
Lions are the only big cats that live in large family groups, (2) ________ are called prides. A typical pride has about ten to fifteen lions, including females and their young cubs.
Female lions, (3) ________ lionesses, do most of the hunting for the pride. They work as a team and can run very fast to catch their prey, such as zebras and wildebeest.
Male lions have a very distinctive thick mane of hair around (4) ________ heads, which makes them look very large and impressive. The darker the mane, the (5) ________ the male lion usually is.
Lions spend up to twenty hours a day resting and sleeping in the shade of trees to save their energy for hunting at night, which is when they are (6) ________ active.

part5.title: Part 5 – Complete Sentences about the Story
part5.instruction: Look at the pictures and read the story. Write 1, 2 or 3 words to complete the sentences about the story. You can use words from the story.

storyPassages.text: Last July, Harry's teacher told the class that they were going on a special two-day school camping trip to the countryside. Harry was incredibly excited because he had never slept in a tent before in his life. On the day of the trip, Harry packed his green rucksack very carefully with everything he needed: warm clothes, a sleeping bag, a torch, and some snacks for the journey.

When they arrived at the campsite next to a beautiful river, all the children helped put up their tents in teams of three. Harry's team worked really well together and had the best tent in the whole campsite! That evening, the teacher made a big campfire and they cooked sausages and roasted marshmallows on sticks. Harry loved the smoky smell and the warm orange glow of the fire.

The next morning, everyone woke up early to go on a long nature walk through the forest with a local wildlife guide called Mr Brown. They saw a deer and a family of rabbits hiding in the long grass. At lunchtime, they sat by the river and ate their sandwiches. Harry said it was the most exciting and unforgettable adventure he had ever had, and he wanted to go camping again every single summer.

In the evening, the teacher made a big ________ for everyone.
The nature walk guide was called ________.
Harry said the camping trip was the most exciting ________ he had ever had.
